incidents.cause: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing. Contributing to the accident was an inadvertent ground-loop.
The student pilot's improper in-flight fuel planning, which resulted in fuel exhaustion.
The pilot receiving instruction’s failure to maintain adequate airspeed and his exceedance of the airplane’s critical angle of attack during takeoff, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.

The failure of both pilots to see and avoid the other airplane while maneuvering in the traffic pattern, which resulted in a midair collision.

The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and to retract the speed brake during the approach, which resulted in a hard landing short of the runway. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor’s decision to conduct a flight review in an airplane without the appropriate visibility,
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a construction sign during taxi operations.
The pilot's decision to depart from a soft grass runway with a tailwind, which resulted in an increased takeoff distance and subsequent impact with trees during the initial climb.
The fatigue failure of the No. 1 cylinder exhaust valve spring retainer due to air trapped in the lubrication system, which resulted in a total loss of engine power.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain airplane control during the landing attempt and the flight instructor’s inadequate remedial action.
